B3: Object-Oriented Programming

SL: 7 hours | HL: 23 hours

Unit Overview

In this unit, you learn how object-oriented programming is used to model real systems. You study classes, objects, methods, constructors, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and class relationships.

Unit Objectives

What students are expected to know:

  • the key ideas behind object-oriented programming
  • how to design and build classes
  • how objects are instantiated and how methods behave
  • how encapsulation and information hiding protect data
  • at HL, how inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction, composition, aggregation and design patterns work across multiple classes

Unit Outcomes

What students are expected to be able to do:

  • evaluate the fundamentals of OOP
  • construct class designs and define objects
  • distinguish between static and non-static members
  • apply encapsulation and information hiding
  • at HL, explain and apply inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction, composition and aggregation
  • explain common design patterns

Subtopics

B3.1

Fundamentals of OOP for a single class — classes, objects, methods, constructors, static and instance members, encapsulation

 B3.2

Fundamentals of OOP for multiple classes (HL only) — inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction, composition, aggregation and design patterns
